traits: White ball without a stem, 10 to 50 cm (up to 80), which can exceed a football
Pure white, even inside when young; yellowish or greenish brown with age
When young, smell of fresh flour
White spores when young, olive when ripe
Meadows rich in droppings of ruminants or birds, sometimes in groups, broadleaf woods · late summer and autumn
safetyNote: Only when young, with pure white, even flesh inside: yellowish or greenish brown, it can cause digestive upset (Wikipedia EN), and it rots within weeks. It is on the German mycological society list and on the Swiss controllers’ list. Wikipedia FR says it can fix heavy metals such as mercury: not in large quantities. Cut it in two: a young amanita egg already shows the future cap and stem; throw it away and wash the knife.
